name: SAINT LUCIA
lead: Saint Lucia is a volcanic Caribbean island famous for the Pitons — two dramatic cones rising straight from the sea. Nicknamed "Helen of the West Indies," it changed hands between Britain and France fourteen times. Today it has rainforests, a drive-in volcano, coral reefs, and banana plantations on every hillside.
geo: Saint Lucia sits between the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic, shaped by ancient volcanoes. The twin Pitons — Gros Piton (770 m) and Petit Piton (743 m) — are a UNESCO World Heritage Site visible far out at sea.

The island's interior is thick tropical rainforest fed by 2,000 mm of rain each year. Sulphur Springs near Soufrière is the world's only drive-in volcano — you park beside bubbling grey mud and smell the hot earth.
animals: Saint Lucia is home to the Saint Lucia Parrot (Jacquot) — a brilliant green bird with red, blue and yellow markings found nowhere else on Earth. Fewer than 150 survived in the 1970s; conservation brought numbers back to over 1,000.

Leatherback sea turtles — heavier than a motorbike — haul themselves up Saint Lucia's beaches each spring to nest. The island's reefs shelter seahorses, flying fish, and the frogfish, which disguises itself as a bumpy rock.
culture: Saint Lucians blend French, African and British traditions. The Creole language Kwéyòl sounds like French through a Caribbean filter and has its own national day — Jounen Kwéyòl — celebrated every October with food, music and storytelling.

The island has two Nobel Prize winners — the most per capita anywhere. Carnival erupts each July with soca music and dazzling costumes. The national dish is green fig and saltfish, and cricket is practically a religion.
history: Indigenous Arawak then Carib people lived here long before Europeans arrived. The island's strategic harbour made it a prize: Britain and France swapped control fourteen times between 1660 and 1814 — a Caribbean record.

Enslaved Africans were brought to work sugar plantations; their descendants form most of today's population. Slavery ended in 1834. Saint Lucia gained full independence on 22 February 1979 and flies its blue-gold Piton flag.
wows: Saint Lucia has 2 Nobel Prize winners — more per capita than any other country on Earth.
The Pitons are so iconic that Saint Lucia can be identified from space by their shape alone.
Sulphur Springs lets you drive a car to within 20 m of boiling volcanic mud — unique on Earth.
The Saint Lucia Parrot rose from 150 birds in 1977 to 1,000+ today thanks to passionate local conservation.
Saint Lucia changed colonial rulers 14 times, leaving French AND British fingerprints on everything.
Bananas grown in volcanic soil here taste noticeably sweeter than most store-bought varieties.
The twin Pitons create a natural windbreak giving Soufrière bay some of the calmest sailing in the Caribbean.

myths.fact: They are two separate volcanic plugs — Gros Piton (770 m) and Petit Piton (743 m) — with a valley between them, though they look merged when viewed from the sea.
Sulphur Springs is a geothermal field of steam vents and boiling mud — dramatic and smelly, but Soufrière last erupted roughly 20,000 years ago.
